title: Prefix caching + batch size sensitivity: onboarding regression notes
content:
Summary:
This doc captures a focused sensitivity sweep we ran during model onboarding for a customer-facing chat model. Goal: quantify latency/cost vs quality when toggling prefix (KV) caching, request batching, and max_tokens caps. This came out of a regression flagged by automated evals where a 2% quality drop coincided with a 20% latency improvement after a runtime change — we wanted to reproduce and attribute.

Key hypotheses:
- Enabling prefix (KV) caching should reduce per-request latency for prompts that share long system/preamble prefixes but may slightly degrade quality if cached keys expire incorrectly or are reused across prompt variants.
- Increasing batch size reduces per-token cost but increases p95 latency; there is a knee point where user-visible latency becomes unacceptable.
- Lowering max_tokens per request reduces tail latency and cost, but can truncate responses and reduce score on longer-turn prompts.

What we ran (high level):
- Models: open-redwood-v2-large (v2025-05-15) and open-redwood-v2-medium (same tag) as the main candidates for onboarding.
- Hardware: Dedicated pool - A100s (single-GPU instances), profile runs vs small-spot T4 for contrast.
- Promptset: 480 chat turn samples (derived from prod-sampled promptset P-042). Includes: 60 short queries (<32 tokens input), 300 medium (32-128), 120 long-context (>128) with ~3 different system/preamble variants to exercise prefix sharing.
- Quality metric(s): combined normalized ROUGE-L for generation clarity + an internal factuality classifier pass rate; we report a composite quality_score = 0.7*ROUGE-NORM + 0.3*Factuality.
- Cost metric: estimated $ per 10k tokens using current pricing abstraction (gpu-time * unit price + fixed infra amortization).
- Latency metrics: p50/p95 server-side response time excluding networking, and token-rate (tokens/sec effective).

Sweep dimensions: (cartesian grid)
- prefix_cache: [off, on, on_prefetch_only] (# on_prefetch_only = pre-seeded cache entries for common prefixes but no dynamic caching)
- batch_size: [1, 4, 8, 16]
- max_tokens_cap: [64, 128, 256]
- kv_cache_ttl_seconds: [60, 300] (only when prefix_cache on)
Total runs: 3 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 2 models x 3 seeds ≈ 864 runs (we parallelized across pools).

Notable results (aggregated):
- Latency: enabling prefix_cache reduced p50 latency by ~18% for medium/long-context samples at batch_size=1, p95 reduced by ~12%. For batch_size >=8 the marginal latency benefit shrank (~5% improvement) because batching dominated scheduling latency.
- Cost: per-token GPU cost decreased 6-14% with prefix_cache on (larger effect for long-context inputs).
- Quality: composite quality_score delta was within ±0.7% for prefix_cache=on vs off across the board, except two prompt families where on_prefetch_only produced a -1.8% drop (likely stale prefetch entries being reused).
- Batch tradeoff: moving from batch_size=1 to 8 reduced cost per token by ~22% but increased p95 latency by 36% for medium prompts. For short prompts, p95 ballooned more (up to 65%) because tail tokens waited for batch completion.
- max_tokens caps: 64 cap reduced cost by ~11% vs 256 but caused a 3.5% drop in quality_score (expected as some reference completions are longer). The user-visible regression risk depends on distribution of target response lengths.

Detailed observations by vector:
- prefix_cache = on_prefetch_only: good cost/latency when prefixes match exactly, but brittle — when prompt minor edits change tokenization of prefix (e.g., punctuation differences), cache misses and occasional reuse of the wrong cache snapshot caused hallucination-like topical shifts in 7 samples. Filed JIRA AIOPS-312.
- kv_cache_ttl 60s vs 300s: shorter TTL reduces stale-reuse issues but also reduces amortization benefits; for medium workloads TTL=300s was sweet spot (balanced cost/quality). For very dynamic prompt sets (customer A/B testing prompts), TTL 60s recommended.
- Batching heuristics: a static batch_size=8 is too aggressive for chat-like flows with many short requests (p95 unacceptable). A dynamic batching policy that caps waiting time (max_wait_ms=7) and adapts batch size by observed prompt length distribution hit a better point: median cost savings close to static 8 but p95 within 1.1x of batch_size=1. Prototype policy implemented in GH PR linked above.

Representative table (summary numbers, medians across samples):
- Model: v2-large, prefix_cache off, batch 1, max 256 -> p50 120ms, p95 480ms, tokens/sec 85, cost/10k $4.8, quality_score 0.882
- Model: v2-large, prefix_cache on, batch 1, max 256 -> p50 98ms, p95 420ms, tokens/sec 98, cost/10k $4.2, quality_score 0.878
- Model: v2-large, prefix_cache on, batch 8, max 256 -> p50 140ms, p95 650ms, tokens/sec 240, cost/10k $3.6, quality_score 0.876
- Model: v2-medium, prefix_cache on, batch 4, max 128 -> p50 85ms, p95 360ms, tokens/sec 140, cost/10k $2.1, quality_score 0.832

Interpretation / recommended defaults for onboarding: (for new customers using chat-like traffic with mix of short+medium prompts)
- Default: prefix_cache = on, kv_cache_ttl = 300s, adaptive batching policy (max_wait_ms 7, max_batch 8), max_tokens default 128 with per-route override. This gives a reliable cost reduction without observable quality regressions for most promptsets we tested.
- Safeguards: enable eval-based regression gating tied to promptset P-042: if composite quality_score drops >1.5% vs baseline under any combination flagged, fail the rollout.
- For customers with highly dynamic prefixes (experiments, interactive editing), set prefix_cache = on_prefetch_only OFF and TTL=60s, or choose prefix_cache=off until we have refined normalization heuristics.

Open questions / action items:
- Need an automated normalizer for prefixes (whitespace/punctuation) before caching to reduce brittle misses. Spike: tokenization-normalizer prototype (Jonah) due 2025-07-02.
- Quantify impact of multi-tenant prefix contamination under shared Dedicated pools — run isolation sim next sprint.
- Validate adaptive batching policy under production traffic (small canary) and instrument cost/latency per-route in Console.
- Investigate the 7 samples with hallucination-like shifts under on_prefetch_only and produce minimal reproducer. Filed AIOPS-312 with examples and logs.

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- push small canary with adaptive batching + prefix_cache=on for 5% of traffic next week.
- add unit test that invalidates prefetch entries when prompt tokens differ beyond threshold.
- update onboarding checklist to include "measure baseline with prefix_cache off" step.

Appendix: quick reproducibility tips
- use run-script: scripts/run_cache_batch_sweep.py --model v2-large --promptset p-042 --out artifacts/prefix_sweep_jun25 --seeds 3
- env: REDWOOD_POOL=dedi-a100-small, RUN_PARALLEL=4
- logs and perf traces available in /gcs/onboard-artifacts/prefix_sweep_jun25 (linked from GH PR).

Bottom line: prefix caching + small adaptive batching yields a favorable cost/latency tradeoff for typical chat workloads with modest or no quality impact. Prefetch-only caches are faster but brittle; TTL tuning and prefix normalization are key mitigations.

-- Priya

(working doc — feedback welcome; planning to convert into a short Confluence decision note if we converge on defaults)
